title: Quality Level Attribution of Existing Utility Records in Four Serbian Municipalities: A Systematic Audit

record.title: Quality Level Attribution of Existing Utility Records in Four Serbian Municipalities: A Systematic Audit
record.abstract: A reliable subsurface utility engineering programme requires knowing the quality level of existing records before planning intrusive works. This paper presents a systematic audit of utility documentation held by four Serbian municipalities covering a combined urban area of approximately 38 km². Records for water, sewerage, gas and electricity were evaluated against a four-tier quality framework adapted from the American CI/ASCE 38-02 standard and calibrated to Serbian regulatory requirements. Auditors reviewed 1,847 plan sheets and 423 digitised GIS layers, assessing completeness, positional accuracy, attribute richness and update frequency. Overall, 31% of reviewed records met quality level B or above; sewerage documentation was the weakest category, with 61% at quality level D. Municipalities with GIS-based cadastres introduced after 2010 performed significantly better than those retaining paper-only systems. The audit protocol is offered as a transferable tool for municipal geodetic services and utility operators preparing investment programmes.
